scope.environment: TokenWrapper ERC20 wrapper contract and off-chain event consumers

entities.name: off-chain indexers, analytics tools, explorers, wallets

statements.text: transferFrom is used with an allowance, so the caller (msg.sender) differs from the token holder (from parameter).
Per ERC20, the Transfer event for transferFrom must use the debited holder address (from) as its first argument, not the caller.
TokenWrapper.transferFrom emits the Transfer event with msg.sender as the from address instead of the from parameter.
Emitted logs misrepresent who actually sent tokens, making event-based balance reconstruction or monitoring incorrect.
Off-chain indexers, analytics tools and block explorers attribute transfers to the approved spender instead of the actual token owner when transferFrom is used.
Infrastructure reconstructing balances purely from events computes incorrect balances for this wrapper token when allowances are used.
No direct on-chain loss of funds occurs; the harm is ERC20 non-compliance breaking integrations.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the caller is authorized or unauthorized; the caller is the approved spender by construction of transferFrom.
No concrete transaction or numeric values are supplied; scenario is described generically.
Wallet/UI misleading history (e_ac6b12e97e08_0008) is a further claimed effect not included among the four impact statements.
